html:
Emperor of Ethiopia from 1434 to 1468 and one of the strongest rulers of the Solomonic dynasty. He ruled the Ethiopian Empire at a high point of royal and church power.

  • He tightened control over provinces and the court, and punished nobles and monks he saw as rebels or heretics.
  • He settled church quarrels on his own terms, ordering both Saturday and Sunday to be kept as holy days and pushing devotion to the Virgin Mary in the Ethiopian Church.
  • He wrote religious books himself, the best known being the Book of Light.
  • He beat the Adal Sultanate in battle in 1445.
  • He founded a new royal seat at Debre Berhan.

Ethiopian monks attended the Council of Florence in 1441 during his reign, a rare contact with Latin Europe. Tradition also places the Ge'ez translation of the Fetha Nagast law code in his time.
